note.data: Bob reported ongoing concerns regarding his workplace performance, stating, "I just feel like I'm dragging everyone down at work." He expressed a belief that his manager is documenting his actions to build a case against him. The therapist and Bob examined the evidence for and against these beliefs. During the session, Bob also disclosed recurring passive suicidal ideation, noting, "sometimes I wonder if everyone would be better off without me." He identified his partner and his dog as significant protective factors.
note.assessment: Bob is currently facing barriers to his goal of reducing self-critical thinking due to persistent all or nothing thinking and feelings of worthlessness. However, he demonstrated progress by engaging in cognitive restructuring to challenge his automatic thoughts. His ability to reach a more balanced thought independently indicates that the treatment framework is effectively weakening his core beliefs of inadequacy.
note.plan: The therapist utilized cognitive restructuring to address automatic thoughts regarding workplace performance. Bob responded well, successfully generating a more balanced perspective on his own. The next clinical step is to continue monitoring risk and practicing thought records between sessions.
client_quotes: I just feel like I'm dragging everyone down at work.
sometimes I wonder if everyone would be better off without me.

next_session_suggestions: Consider reviewing the evidence for his belief that his manager is building a case against him.
Possible focus on identifying other areas of life where Bob feels competent to counter the worthlessness theme.

note.data: Marcus reported on his current medication transition from sertraline to escitalopram (10mg), noting that the previous medication made him feel "flat" and numb. He described experiencing a return of anticipatory worry in the mornings during this transition period. The therapist and client discussed his symptoms of generalized anxiety and low mood, which remain active. Marcus stated that "having a concrete plan for the morning actually helps" regarding his current routine.
note.assessment: Marcus is currently maintaining rather than gaining ground toward his treatment goals due to the medication switch acting as a clinical barrier. The return of anticipatory worry aligns with the pharmacological transition. Progress on mood goals is currently hindered by these systemic changes, but he remains engaged in planning.
note.plan: The therapist utilized behavioral activation to develop a morning routine for Marcus. Marcus responded well to this intervention, expressing that having a concrete plan provides some relief from his dread. The next clinical step is to monitor the stabilization of symptoms as the escitalopram beds in.
client_quotes: having a concrete plan for the morning actually helps

actions.purpose: Follow up to monitor medication transition

next_session_suggestions: Consider reviewing the effectiveness of the morning behavioral activation plan.
Possible focus on monitoring specific side effects or improvements with the escitalopram transition.
Consider exploring the content of the anticipatory worry to identify specific automatic thoughts.

note.data: Jane presented for her individual session and reported feeling hooked on the thought that she would fail an upcoming work presentation. The therapist facilitated cognitive defusion exercises where Jane practiced noticing and naming the thought as "I'm having the thought that I'll fail" to create space from it. During this process, Jane stated, "my thoughts are just noise, they're not instructions." The session then transitioned into values clarification, identifying her desire to be seen as competent and to contribute at work. She discussed her willingness to experience anxiety in order to live out these values rather than avoiding the discomfort of the presentation.
note.assessment: Jane is demonstrating significant progress toward her treatment goals of acceptance and cognitive defusion. Her ability to recognize thoughts as mental events rather than directives indicates a successful shift in her relationship with anxious content. By connecting her willingness to endure anxiety directly to her core values, she is moving from avoidance-based behavior toward committed action. Her consistent adherence to the sleep wind-down routine suggests maintenance of previous gains.
note.plan: The therapist utilized cognitive defusion and values clarification to address presentation-related anxiety. Jane responded well by successfully unhooking from catastrophic thoughts and identifying her underlying drivers for work performance. The next clinical step is to continue mapping her values and monitoring the application of these skills during the upcoming work deadline.
client_quotes: my thoughts are just noise, they're not instructions
I'm having the thought that I'll fail

actions.purpose: warm check in and values mapping homework

next_session_suggestions: Consider reviewing the outcomes of the work presentation using a defusion lens.
Possible focus on further expanding the values map to other areas of life.

note.data: Rosa attended the session alone to discuss family dynamics involving her husband and her teenage son, Leo. The therapist and client identified a pattern of triangulation where Rosa acts as a messenger during conflicts between her husband and son. Rosa reported, "I always end up in the middle between them." The session focused on mapping this triangle and identifying how Rosa stabilizes it by carrying messages back and forth. Discussion also centered on blurred boundaries between the parental subsystem and their child, noting significant enmeshment between Rosa and Leo. Rosa stated, "when he's upset I feel like it's my job to fix it immediately."
note.assessment: Rosa is making early progress toward her goal of improving family dynamics by increasing her awareness of her role in the triangulation pattern. However, she faces barriers to change as she continues to instinctively stabilize the triangle and struggles with enmeshment. The client demonstrated improved insight into how her actions maintain the current system.
note.plan: The therapist used mapping of the triangulation pattern to illustrate family dynamics. Rosa responded by identifying her specific role as a messenger. The next clinical step is to move toward differentiation by practicing stepping out of the middle and allowing the husband and son to interact directly.
client_quotes: I always end up in the middle between them
when he's upset I feel like it's my job to fix it immediately

actions.purpose: Family session with husband and son present

unsupported_requests: have the husband and Leo in the room next time
next_session_suggestions: Consider exploring specific ways Rosa can resist the urge to carry messages between her husband and son.
Possible focus on identifying specific moments of enmeshment with Leo to practice setting boundaries.

note.data: Tom arrived late due to parking difficulties and spent the initial portion of the session venting about his commute. He reported that the commute serves as a primary trigger for catastrophizing, stating, "by the time I get to my desk I've already imagined getting fired three times." The therapist and client mapped this automatic thought pattern from the drive into a thought record. Tom noted that "writing it down makes it look kind of ridiculous." Additionally, Tom reported improved sleep and indicated that previous behavioral activation strategies, such as walking during lunch, are proving helpful.
note.assessment: Tom is making decent progress toward his goal of managing catastrophizing and identifying automatic thoughts earlier. He demonstrated increased awareness of the link between his commute and his anxiety. His engagement with the thought record suggests a positive shift in perspective regarding the validity of his fears.
note.plan: The therapist utilized cognitive restructuring through a thought record to address catastrophizing. Tom responded well, showing movement by recognizing the irrationality of his thoughts when documented. The next clinical step is to continue monitoring these triggers and refining the thought record process.
client_quotes: by the time I get to my desk I've already imagined getting fired three times.
writing it down makes it look kind of ridiculous.

next_session_suggestions: Consider continuing to map specific triggers during the commute using thought records.
Possible focus on identifying other areas of work stress where catastrophizing occurs.
